purpose: Engineering-only assessment of whether checkout memory ceilings near observed consumption bind under a fixed CPU allocation and workload. Not a joint-resource hypothesis test or a campaign replication.
range_rationale: The earlier fixed path ended at 64 MiB without observed memory-cap events; measured checkout peaks were approximately 25--35 MiB. The fixed grid brackets that consumption, with 64/48/40 MiB headroom points and 36/32/28/24/20 MiB lower ceilings. All points run, irrespective of outcomes.
execution: Nine independent fresh runners. Each restores the same initially safe 256-MiB checkout baseline, then applies one RAM-only allocation or an unchanged sham control. Recipient memory equals 768 MiB minus checkout memory. CPU, workloads, code, Go memory settings and restart policy remain unchanged.
failure_rule: Latency/errors alone determine the SLO label. Post-intervention OOM/restart never changes it or automatically excludes the point. Record update errors, confirm persisted/live configuration, and preserve every readable primary outcome. Missing primary data or confirmed resource mismatch is technical-invalid.
analysis: Report all nine conditions, raw memory-cap events, Docker OOM diagnostics, external SLO outcomes and validity. One observation per limit does not establish a reproducible safe threshold, causality, alert accuracy or monotonicity. No fitted model, binary scientific criterion, outcome-based replacement or automatic follow-on campaign.
